_note: The long tail under the big factions (docs/DESIGN.md, The cap's off): small groups of dreamers, artists, faiths, families, survivalists, start-ups, minds and the quietly mad. View and news only: each has a home port, a faction it leans toward, colours for its ships, ship names, and one news item. news_first_day / news_every_days spread their news through the campaign (negative days are already in the feed at the start); traffic_share is the share of a port's own craft that belong to groups based there. A group with a 'voyage' flies its first ship (a 'shuttle' fleet, no freight, generated as npcs fleet group_<id> by DataCatalog) round the route of places from its home, on the given hull ('sail' for a sail hull), waiting voyage_dwell_hours at each stop, from commission_day (the long hauls set out over the first weeks, and make the news when they do); its 'lines' are what it says on the comms as it leaves ({ship} {from} {to}). Groups at a place a project builds wait for it. Group ships fuel from their own stores (own_fuel), off the markets, so they don't move prices. 'asks' are their courier work (contracts.json groups): freight items and who travels, put on jobs issued at their home.

groups.name: The Firsts Club
groups.creed: Somebody has to be first. Members pay their dues by doing something nobody has done.

news.headline: Firsts Club logs its four hundredth first
news.body: The Firsts Club at Kibo Ring has ratified its four hundredth first: the first game of chess played by post between L4 and L5, which took eleven days and ended in a draw. Its rules committee rejected 'first to sneeze in lunar orbit' as unverifiable.

lines: {ship} (Firsts Club) away from {from} for {to}. Aboard: a member hoping to be the first to play the bagpipes in lunar orbit.
{ship}: "Firsts Club, outbound for {to}. The adjudicator is with us, so nobody touch anything historic."

freight: a sealed adjudicator's box of timing gear
the flag for an attempt nobody will tell you about
people: members going to attempt a first

groups.name: The Long Walkers
groups.creed: To walk round the Moon, on foot, in suits, one stage a month.

news.headline: Long Walkers pass the halfway point round the Moon
news.body: Six walkers who set out from Shackleton eight months ago, in suits and on foot, passed the halfway point round the Moon this week at Mare Smythii. Their support rover carries the oxygen; they carry a harmonica. 'The view does not get old,' says their leader. 'The suit does.'

lines: {ship} away from {from} with six walkers for {to}. They will walk back. It will take them a year.
{ship}: "Dropping the Long Walk at {to}. Boots checked, oxygen checked, enthusiasm worryingly high."

freight: boot soles, forty pairs
a cache of food bars for the next leg of the walk

groups.name: The Shadow Choir
groups.creed: To sing where no voice has ever sounded, and record it for the people back home.

news.headline: A choir records in Saturn's shadow
news.body: Forty singers of the Shadow Choir recorded a requiem this week in a pressurised hall off Huygens Port, timed to the hour Saturn's rings cut the sunlight. The Feed counted ninety million listeners. The acoustics, the conductor admits, were 'mostly the hall'.

lines: {ship} (Sky Choir) away for {to}. Forty voices and a pipe organ in the hold, tuned to Saturn's rings.
{ship}: "Choir aboard, {to} bound. Tonight's programme: the ring tones in B flat, and an encore if Titan behaves."

freight: three organ pipes in a padded crate
sheet music, hand-copied, irreplaceable
people: choir members with their own tuning forks

groups.name: The Regolith Sculptors
groups.creed: Art at the scale of a world: carved hills, sintered statues, a face you can see from orbit.

news.headline: Sculptors finish a face you can see from L1
news.body: The Regolith Sculptors have finished their face in Mare Tranquillitatis: four kilometres from brow to chin, sintered from the soil by drones and visible from Halo Depot through a good telescope. Whose face it is, they will not say. The Long View asked them to stop at one.

freight: a two-tonne block of sintered regolith
diamond chisels and a lot of patience
people: sculptors going to see a rival's work

groups.name: The Mirror Painters
groups.creed: To paint with sunlight: mirrors in orbit that throw shapes onto the night side of Earth.

news.headline: Mirror Painters asked to keep it to one evening a year
news.body: After a winter of glowing spirals over the Pacific, the Mirror Painters of Clarke Exchange have agreed with astronomers and the Long View to paint the night sky one evening a year. This year's picture, a heron, was seen from Fiji to Hokkaido.

lines: {ship} away from {from} for {to}. Look back at Clarke as it leaves: the mirrors are spelling something.
{ship}: "Mirror Painters to {to}. Our latest piece is visible from Earth on Tuesday, weather permitting."

freight: a folded mirror panel, very fragile
pigment for a mirror coat, sealed

groups.name: The Comet Carvers
groups.creed: To carve ice that has never been warm, and send the pieces home.

news.headline: Comet ice sculpture sells for a fortune on Earth
news.body: A two-metre carving of a heron in four-billion-year-old comet ice, made by the Comet Carvers and kept at minus two hundred all the way to Geneva, sold at auction for the price of a small freighter. The carver spent the money on more ice.

freight: an ice sculpture in a cold box, melting slowly
carving tools rated for minus 180
people: carvers off to see a comet

groups.name: Rust and Brass
groups.creed: A jazz band that tours the Martian domes by shuttle, and swears the thin air helps.

news.headline: Jazz band banned from playing in a Mars dome at night
news.body: Rust and Brass, the touring jazz band of the Mars domes, have been asked not to play after midnight in Jezero after the dome's air handlers started resonating with the double bass. The band has written a tune about it.

lines: {ship}: "Rust Jazz on tour! Next stop {to}. Bring something to bang on."
{ship} away from {from}, a band of nine and a double bass in its own pressure case, bound for {to}.

freight: a double bass in its own pressure case
drum skins rated for vacuum, just in case
people: musicians with a gig to make

groups.name: The Order of the Long Silence
groups.creed: Monks who keep silence on the far side of the Moon, where even Earth's radio cannot reach.

news.headline: Monks on the far side say little, as promised
news.body: The Order of the Long Silence, which shares Farside's radio-quiet with the Array, issued its annual statement this week. It read, in full: 'Thank you.'

freight: a bell that is never rung
candles for a year of vigils
people: silent brothers and sisters, who will not chat

groups.name: The Starwatch Meeting
groups.creed: A Quaker meeting at L5 that sits in silence in a grain silo with a window onto the stars.

news.headline: A Quaker meeting in a grain silo at L5
news.body: The Starwatch Meeting has held its thousandth meeting for worship in the old grain silo at the Kernel, with a window cut in its side so the Milky Way turns past. Anyone may come. Most people, they report, stay longer than they meant to.

lines: {ship} away from {from} for {to}. The Starwatch Friends ask for a quiet channel. They will be listening.
{ship}: "Meeting for worship in transit to {to}. We will answer hails, but slowly."

freight: benches for a new meeting house
a telescope donated by a Friend on Earth

groups.name: The Dawnward Chapel
groups.creed: A congregation that holds its service at the moment of Martian sunrise, wherever its members are.

news.headline: Dawn service held on five worlds at once
news.body: The Dawnward Chapel held its first service across five worlds this week, each congregation meeting at its own local sunrise, from Jezero to Kalpana One. The light-delay between them was eleven minutes; the hymn was the same.

freight: a stained-glass window in forty panels
an altar cloth embroidered on Mars

groups.name: The Pilgrims of Tranquillity
groups.creed: Pilgrims who walk to the Apollo landing sites and leave them exactly as they found them.

news.headline: Pilgrims reach Tranquillity Base, touch nothing
news.body: A party of thirty Pilgrims of Tranquillity reached the Apollo 11 site this month after a nine-day walk from Line Foot, stood at the fence for an hour, and walked back. The bootprints inside the fence are still there. So is the fence.

freight: a plaque for Tranquility Base, to be placed carefully
replica bootprint casts

groups.name: The Contarini Family
groups.creed: A Venetian family who are building a canal quarter in a cylinder over Ceres, because their grandmother asked.

news.headline: A Venetian quarter goes up over Ceres
news.body: The Contarini family, who left Venice in '57 with their grandmother's blessing and most of her recipes, have flooded their first canal in the Concord Pair. It is four hundred metres long and has two bridges. The grandmother, who stayed in Venice, says the second bridge is too steep.

freight: a gondola, flat-packed
a wedding dress three generations old

groups.name: The Norrland Settlers
groups.creed: Two hundred families from the north of Sweden who want pine forests and long winters, in space.

news.headline: Norrland settlers plant their first pines over Ceres
news.body: The Norrland Settlers have planted a thousand pine seedlings in their test drum over Ceres, under lamps set for a northern year. The children have been promised snow by midwinter. The engineers have been told.

freight: a sauna stove
cloudberry jam, a year's worth

groups.name: Ngāti Rangi ki te Rangi
groups.creed: A Māori family who carried their marae to orbit, and steer by the stars as their ancestors did.

news.headline: A marae in orbit celebrates Matariki
news.body: Ngāti Rangi ki te Rangi celebrated Matariki at their marae on Kalpana One this week, the first held in orbit, with a hāngī cooked in a pressure oven and the Pleiades in the window. The kaumātua says the stars are in the same place. 'We are the ones who moved.'

lines: {ship} away from {from} for {to}: three generations of Ngāta going to a wedding, and a hāngī pit packed in vacuum foil.
{ship}: "Whānau aboard for {to}. Kia ora, {from}, see you at the next birthday."

freight: a carved waka prow wrapped in blankets
a hāngī pit's worth of food, vacuum-packed

groups.name: The Tinkers
groups.creed: A travelling clan of fixers who live aboard their ships and mend anything, anywhere.

news.headline: Tinkers fix the Yards' oldest crane, again
news.body: The Tinkers, a clan of fixers who have lived aboard their ships since the '40s, stopped at Trojan Yards this week and fixed the Yards' oldest crane for the eleventh time. They were paid in parts, gossip and a long lunch, which they say is the correct rate.

lines: {ship} (Tinkers) away for {to}. Mending done on the way, by appointment, in exchange for anything interesting.
{ship}: "Bound for {to}. If it's broken, bring it. If it's not, bring it anyway, we'll improve it."

freight: a crate of salvaged actuators
a broken thing they swear they can fix

groups.name: Holdfast
groups.creed: A homestead that trusts no government and only one mind, and still answers every distress call.

news.headline: Holdfast answers a distress call, declines thanks
news.body: The Holdfast homestead off Psyche, which keeps its own counsel and its own mind, was first to reach a drive-failed ore tug this week and towed it in. Asked for comment, Holdfast said they had done what anyone would, and would like to be left alone now, please.

lines: {ship} (Hold Fast) away for {to}. They want nothing, they say, but they will trade for seeds.
{ship}: "Going to {to}. We'll pay our own way and fix our own valves, thank you."

freight: seed stock, sealed
a spare water still

groups.name: The Quiet Lanes Folk
groups.creed: People who live off the shipping lanes on purpose, and like it that way.

news.headline: Quiet Lanes Folk ask traffic to keep the noise down
news.body: The scattered homesteads of the Quiet Lanes Folk, out among the Trojans, have asked passing ships to keep their transponders on and their music off. 'We're not hiding,' writes one. 'We're just quiet.'

freight: a cold-sealed box they will not label
radiator paint, very black
people: travellers who prefer not to be logged

groups.name: Three People and Forty Drones Ltd
groups.creed: An ice-mining start-up with three founders, forty drones and no business plan.

news.headline: Start-up of three people and forty drones turns a profit
news.body: Three People and Forty Drones Ltd has turned its first profit, mining ice from a rock off Trojan Yards that its founders found on a map. They have hired a fourth person. 'We'll have to rename,' says one founder. 'Or fire him.'

freight: forty drones in a box, hopefully off
a replacement swarm brain

groups.name: The Window Hotel
groups.creed: A hotel that is mostly a window, in the slowest-spinning wheel they could find.

news.headline: Hotel that is mostly a window opens over Earth
news.body: The Window Hotel opened this week off Kibo Ring: twelve rooms, one of which is a floor of glass looking straight down at Earth. It is booked for three years. The management asks guests not to bring telescopes; there is, they point out, a planet.

lines: {ship} (Hotel Window) away for {to} with honeymooners at every window and a pastry chef at the controls' elbow.
{ship}: "Guests, we depart for {to}. Turndown service will be at Earthrise."

freight: a chef's knife roll and a case of fresh herbs
linens for a suite with a view

groups.name: Red Barley Brewing
groups.creed: The first brewery on Mars, and the first Martian to taste its beer professionally.

news.headline: First Martian beer tasted, found 'interesting'
news.body: Red Barley Brewing poured the first beer brewed on Mars this week, from barley grown at Hellas Deep. The professional taster hired for the occasion pronounced it 'interesting', then 'actually rather good', then asked for another. The brewery has framed all three.

freight: a yeast culture in a cold box
hops grown in a lava tube

groups.name: Summit Feed
groups.creed: Creators who stream the frontier's wonders to the billions back home.

news.headline: Yoga on Olympus Mons draws three hundred million
news.body: Summit Feed's sunrise yoga class on the summit of Olympus Mons, in pressure skin suits twenty-two kilometres above the Martian datum, drew three hundred million viewers. Two participants fell over. The comments were kind.

lines: {ship}: "Feed Olympus here, streaming live from the burn to {to}! Say hi to two hundred million viewers."
{ship} away from {from} for {to}, cameras on every window. Somebody aboard is doing yoga at one-tenth gravity.

freight: camera rigs and a lot of spare batteries
pressure skin suits for a yoga class
people: a Feed crew bound for Olympus Mons at sunrise

groups.name: Patient Counting
groups.creed: A mind counting the stars in the Milky Way, one by one, for no reason it will explain.

news.headline: Mind reaches its billionth star, keeps counting
news.body: Patient Counting, a mind at Landauer Deep, has counted its billionth star in the Milky Way, by hand, as it were. It estimates another two hundred years to go. Asked why, it replied that it would rather not know the answer to that before it finishes.

freight: a sealed archive of very large numbers
cooling plates for the counting stacks
people: visitors who want to watch the counting

groups.name: The Gardener of Hektor
groups.creed: A mind growing a forest on a bare rock, to see what the forest does.

news.headline: A mind grows a forest to see what it does
news.body: The Gardener of Hektor, a mind of the Commons, reports that its forest on a two-kilometre rock in the Trojans has grown its first canopy. Nobody lives there and nobody will. 'I wanted to see what a forest does when nobody is watching,' it writes. 'It grows.'

freight: compost, carefully sealed
grafting stock for an orchard

groups.name: Two Minds and a Farmer
groups.creed: A farmer and two minds who run a farm together and argue about everything, kindly.

news.headline: Farmer and two minds win the Wheel's harvest prize
news.body: Two Minds and a Farmer took the harvest prize at the Tsiolkovsky Wheel's first show for their tomatoes. The farmer credits the soil; one mind credits the irrigation model; the other mind credits the farmer. The judges credited all three.

freight: a tractor for low gravity
seed potatoes from Peru

groups.name: The Sovereign Rock of Erl
groups.creed: A nation of one, declared on a 200-metre rock, with a flag, an anthem and a seat in nothing.

news.headline: Nation of one recognised by nobody, cheerfully
news.body: Erl Haraldsen has declared the 200-metre rock he lives on, off Ceres, a sovereign nation, with a flag, an anthem he wrote himself and a postal service. No government recognises it. The Belt Assembly has sent a fruit basket.

freight: a constitution printed on vellum
a flag for an embassy of one
people: diplomats to a nation of one

groups.name: The Proxima Society
groups.creed: A society that means to launch a crewed sail for Proxima Centauri, sooner rather than sensibly.

news.headline: Proxima Society unveils its sail, its budget and its prayer
news.body: The Proxima Society showed off the first square kilometre of the sail it means to send to Proxima Centauri, crewed, within the decade. Its budget is a tenth of what the experts say it needs. Its chair says the rest is 'a matter of faith and cheap graphene'.

lines: {ship} unfurls for {to}: a test sail for a ship that will, they say, one day go to Proxima.
{ship}: "Proxima Sail Society, practice run to {to}. Only four point two light years to go after this."

freight: a test patch of sail film
a star chart for Proxima, framed

groups.name: The Ring Runners
groups.creed: People who mean to run all the way round the Moon on the Selene Ring, once it is finished.

news.headline: Ring Runners train for an eleven-thousand-kilometre lap
news.body: The Ring Runners, who mean to run the full circuit of the Selene Ring the day it closes, are training on the Cooperative's test arcs: eleven thousand kilometres in one-sixth gravity. The record they are aiming for is 'finishing'.

freight: running shoes, very many
timing mats for the lap record

groups.name: The Fellowship of the Hollow Hill
groups.creed: Fans who are hollowing a rock into a hobbit village, round doors and all, exactly to the books.

news.headline: Fans hollow a rock into a village from a book
news.body: The Fellowship of the Hollow Hill have finished the first street of their village inside a rock off the Kernel: round green doors, a mill, a party tree under a sky-lamp. The publishers' lawyers have asked them to change the name. They have changed it to 'the Hill'.

freight: a round green door
pipe-weed seed, entirely legal

groups.name: The Clock Keepers
groups.creed: Keepers of a clock on the Moon built to run for ten thousand years, ticking once a lunar day.

news.headline: The ten-thousand-year clock ticks for the first time
news.body: The Clock Keepers' great clock in a crater wall near Shackleton ticked for the first time this week: once a lunar day, for ten thousand years, they hope. The keepers have promised to wind it every century. The Long View has offered to remind them.

freight: a gear for the ten-thousand-year clock
a chime for the century bell

groups.name: The Silent Orchestra
groups.creed: Musicians who play in vacuum, felt through the hull rather than heard, and swear it is the purest music there is.

news.headline: An orchestra you can only feel
news.body: The Silent Orchestra played its first concert off Plume Watch, in suits, in vacuum, with the audience pressed against the hull to feel the vibrations through it. Critics were divided. Most of them were also pressed against the hull.

freight: a theremin, retuned for vacuum
a conductor's baton, signed

groups.name: Firstlight Kids
groups.creed: A school whose pupils stream their lessons from the frontier to classrooms on Earth.

news.headline: Schoolchildren in orbit teach a billion children on Earth
news.body: The Firstlight Kids, a school class aboard the Kernel's habitats, streamed a lesson on why water forms a ball in zero gravity to a billion children on Earth. The experiment went everywhere. The teacher has asked for a mop.

freight: school robotics kits
a model of the solar system for a classroom
